./memory-armed.json#json.$doc: J426 (Jake, 2026-11-18): the one armed-zone list. A zone named here has done the work to get under the J410 lines, and from then on every memory gate refuses it back over them, with no override flag and no report-only fallback: the format's offline estimate over lines.playingBytes / lines.loadingBytes (check, validate, cook, upload), the declared worst-location total over the J408 1.5 GB line, the runtime tier and a stale runtime reading; engine's ledger, footprint and boot-line guards read the same list. A zone not named here reports only (J424). Each zone's playingBytes / loadingBytes are its offline estimate when it was armed (memory epoch in `epoch`); the offline estimate refuses over the larger of the line and that reading plus 0.5% (memory-armed.ts ARMED_ALLOWANCE), so a zone EM11 measured under the line whose conservative estimate reads over it (Nine's playing) is locked at its armed state. Decimal bytes. Format memory-armed.ts reads this; engine reads @wildshard/format/src/format/memory-armed.json. CP10 judges a stored original by its stored verdict, so no pinned product is re-judged and nothing is held (FORMAT-PRUNE FP12): the four zones once held (Driftwood, Nalati, Nine Dragon, Pine) are armed again at their epoch-8 readings (SHARD-COMPAT CP10, after Pine r10 and Nalati r5 pinned), and only a new upload over a line is refused. Nine Dragon is held again (SHARD-COMPAT SM4, 2026-11-22): its main source reads 1,963.9 MB loading offline (runtime, commons and boot included) against the 1.5 GB ceiling, so its next upload would be refused; it reports only (J424) until its source is under the line, then re-arms. Arming moves to the API catalogue at FP27.
